chains.trait: Elongated, digitigrade saltatorial hindlimbs with fused metatarsals
links: Open prairie offers zero cover; survival demands explosive acceleration
Reduced gravity lowers the energetic cost of high-striding gallops
Masseteric muscle tendons store kinetic energy for ballistic leaps
Predator pack coordination forces vertical evasion over lateral flight

skill.effect: Increases movement range by 50% on open ground for 1 turn.

chains.weakness: Cannot turn quickly; momentum carries them straight, making them vulnerable to flank attacks on slopes.
observe: Legs coil like springs before a burst leap
Fused metatarsals act as rigid levers for ground push
Herds move in unison, exploiting each other's slipstreams

journal.en: The prey burned their brains to save calories; now they run on instinct, a herd of legs and panic.

analogues.organism: Macropodidae (red kangaroo, Macropus rufus)—elongated hindfoot, elastic Achilles/storage of strain energy in tendons; artiodactyl fused metapodials as rigid distal lever (cannon bone).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

chains.trait: Smaller cranial volume and fused manual digits
links: The 'spark' of mind is energetically costly and irrelevant for fleeing herbivores
Qu-engineered synthetic proteins were pruned in fertile grasslands
Unused neural tissue generates excess heat and drains caloric intake
Caloric surplus diverted to digestive symbionts over cortical expansion

skill.effect: Herd movement reduces predator aggro range by 10% for adjacent allies.

chains.weakness: Cannot be taught tools or tricks; confused by non-patterned traps and isolated from the herd.
observe: Eyes lack focused intent; gaze drifts randomly across the horizon
Cranial ridge recedes, leaving a blunt forehead
Calves nurse longer but grow faster than full-brained ancestors

journal.en: Nothing is sacred in the evolutionary process; the mind is the first luxury shed when the grass is green.

plausibility.summary: Fused digits read better as vestigial posthuman manual morphology under relaxed selection ( syndactyly/reduced ray count ) than as an active hop adaptation—tie explicitly to F17 brain-size selection and F18 grass nitrogen economics.
fixes: Fused digits read better as vestigial posthuman manual morphology under relaxed selection ( syndactyly/reduced ray count ) than as an active hop adaptation—tie explicitly to F17 brain-size selection and F18 grass nitrogen economics.

analogues.organism: Domestication brain-size reduction (silver fox, Canidae selection experiment; reduced endocranial volume in domestic ungulates); "expensive tissue" trade-off between brain and gut.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Predators triangulate prey footfalls with independently rotating pinnae; prey counter with silent digitigrade leaping across prairie grasses.
Divergent neural retention; Mantelopes retain human encephalic volume at high metabolic cost, while prey prune neural tissue for faster grazing and survival.
Aerial Flyers dive on prairie herds, selecting for Saltatorial Prey's high-speed leaping gait and vigilance.
